title: Case Study: ATM
summary: Design an ATM end to end — entities, the State pattern for its session flow, cash dispensing, and the edge cases interviewers probe for.

blocks.markdown:
An **ATM** is a favorite LLD interview question because it's a **session** with strict ordering: you can't withdraw before authenticating, and can't authenticate before inserting a card. That ordering is the whole design.

- Core entities: `ATM`, `Card`, `Account`, `BankService`, `CashDispenser`, a `Transaction`, and a `State`.
- The twist interviewers want: model the session with the **State pattern**, not a pile of flags.
- See [behavioral-patterns-i](behavioral-patterns-i) for State's general shape; [lld-interview-framework](lld-interview-framework) for the approach.

blocks.subTitle: Requirements
blocks.markdown:
What the machine must support.

| Functional | Edge cases |
|---|---|
| Insert card, authenticate PIN | Wrong PIN (limited attempts) |
| Check balance | Card retained after too many tries |
| Withdraw cash | Insufficient account funds |
| Deposit cash | Insufficient ATM cash for withdrawal |
| Eject card | Concurrent session on one machine |

Every row on the right becomes a **transition rule** in the state machine, not a special-case `if`.

blocks.subTitle: From nouns to classes
blocks.markdown:
Pick out the nouns in the requirements and turn each into a class with a clear job.

- **Card** — card number, linked account id. Read when inserted.
- **Account** — balance, PIN hash. The bank owns the truth, not the ATM.
- **BankService** — the backend the ATM calls to authenticate a PIN and check/update balance over the network.
- **CashDispenser** — physical cash inventory by denomination; breaks a withdrawal amount into notes.
- **ATM** — the **context**: holds current state, inserted card, and entered amount.

blocks.subTitle: Model the session as states
blocks.markdown:
The naive design tracks a `status` field and checks it everywhere: `if status == "AUTHENTICATED" and status != "DISPENSING"...`. Every new rule touches every method.

- The fix: each stage of the session becomes its **own class** implementing one `ATMState` interface.
- `ATM` never asks "what state am I in" — it just calls `state.insertCard()`, `state.enterPin()`, `state.selectTransaction()`, and the **current state object** decides what happens and what state comes next.
- This is the **State pattern**: behavior varies by internal state, and the state itself drives the transition.

blocks.subTitle: Card & Account
blocks.markdown:
```text
class Card:
    field cardNumber
    field accountId

    constructor(cardNumber, accountId):
        this.cardNumber = cardNumber
        this.accountId = accountId

class Account:
    field accountId
    field balance
    field pinHash

    method hasSufficientFunds(amount):
        return this.balance >= amount

    method debit(amount):
        this.balance -= amount

    method credit(amount):
        this.balance += amount
```

blocks.subTitle: BankService (backend)
blocks.markdown:
```text
// the ATM never trusts its own copy of balance/PIN — it always asks the bank
interface BankService:
    method authenticate(cardNumber, pin) -> boolean
    method getBalance(accountId) -> amount
    method withdraw(accountId, amount) -> boolean   // false if insufficient funds
    method deposit(accountId, amount)

class RemoteBankService implements BankService:
    method authenticate(cardNumber, pin):
        return httpCall("/auth", cardNumber, hash(pin))

    method getBalance(accountId):
        return httpCall("/balance", accountId)

    method withdraw(accountId, amount):
        return httpCall("/withdraw", accountId, amount)   // bank checks funds atomically

    method deposit(accountId, amount):
        httpCall("/deposit", accountId, amount)
```

blocks.subTitle: The State interface
blocks.markdown:
```text
interface ATMState:
    method insertCard(atm, card)
    method enterPin(atm, pin)
    method selectTransaction(atm, transaction)
    method ejectCard(atm)

// default behavior: reject the action if the current state doesn't support it
abstract class BaseState implements ATMState:
    method insertCard(atm, card):
        print("Cannot insert card now")
    method enterPin(atm, pin):
        print("Cannot enter PIN now")
    method selectTransaction(atm, transaction):
        print("Cannot select transaction now")
    method ejectCard(atm):
        print("No card to eject")
```

blocks.subTitle: IdleState & CardInsertedState
blocks.markdown:
```text
class IdleState extends BaseState:
    method insertCard(atm, card):
        atm.currentCard = card
        atm.setState(new CardInsertedState())

class CardInsertedState extends BaseState:
    field attempts = 0
    static field MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3

    method enterPin(atm, pin):
        if atm.bank.authenticate(atm.currentCard.cardNumber, pin):
            atm.setState(new AuthenticatedState())
        else:
            this.attempts += 1
            if this.attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS:
                print("Too many attempts — retaining card")
                atm.retainCard()
                atm.setState(new IdleState())
            else:
                print("Wrong PIN, try again")   // stays in this state

    method ejectCard(atm):
        atm.returnCard()
        atm.setState(new IdleState())
```

blocks.subTitle: Transaction hierarchy
blocks.markdown:
```text
// Template Method: fixed run() skeleton, subclasses fill in the one step that differs
abstract class Transaction:
    field accountId
    field amount

    method run(atm):
        if this.execute(atm):
            print("Transaction complete")
        else:
            print("Transaction failed")

    abstract method execute(atm) -> boolean

class WithdrawTransaction extends Transaction:
    method execute(atm):
        if not atm.bank.withdraw(this.accountId, this.amount):
            return false                 // bank says insufficient funds
        if not atm.dispenser.canDispense(this.amount):
            atm.bank.deposit(this.accountId, this.amount)   // compensate: put funds back
            return false
        atm.dispenser.dispense(this.amount)
        return true

class DepositTransaction extends Transaction:
    method execute(atm):
        atm.bank.deposit(this.accountId, this.amount)
        return true

class BalanceInquiry extends Transaction:
    method execute(atm):
        print("Balance: " + atm.bank.getBalance(this.accountId))
        return true
```

blocks.subTitle: AuthenticatedState & TransactionState
blocks.markdown:
```text
class AuthenticatedState extends BaseState:
    method selectTransaction(atm, transaction):
        atm.setState(new TransactionState())
        atm.state.run(transaction, atm)   // proceed immediately

    method ejectCard(atm):
        atm.returnCard()
        atm.setState(new IdleState())

class TransactionState extends BaseState:
    method run(transaction, atm):
        transaction.run(atm)
        atm.setState(new AuthenticatedState())   // back to menu for another transaction

    // selectTransaction/enterPin/insertCard all rejected here — a transaction is mid-flight
```

blocks.subTitle: CashDispenser (note breakdown)
blocks.markdown:
```text
enum Denomination:
    NOTE_100, NOTE_500, NOTE_2000

class CashDispenser:
    field trayCounts = map()   // Denomination -> count in the machine
    static field VALUE = { NOTE_100: 100, NOTE_500: 500, NOTE_2000: 2000 }

    method totalCash():
        return sum(VALUE[d] * trayCounts[d] for d in trayCounts)

    method canDispense(amount):
        return amount <= this.totalCash() and this.breakInto(amount) != null

    // greedy, largest note first; a real ATM also respects per-tray counts
    method breakInto(amount):
        plan = map()
        for d in sortDescending(Denomination.values(), by=VALUE):
            available = trayCounts[d]
            count = min(available, amount / VALUE[d])
            plan[d] = count
            amount -= count * VALUE[d]
        if amount > 0:
            return null            // can't make exact amount with what's left
        return plan

    method dispense(amount):
        plan = this.breakInto(amount)
        for d in plan:
            trayCounts[d] -= plan[d]
        print("Dispensing: " + plan)
```

blocks.subTitle: ATM (the context)
blocks.markdown:
```text
class ATM:
    field state = new IdleState()
    field bank            // BankService
    field dispenser        // CashDispenser
    field currentCard = null

    method setState(state):
        this.state = state

    method retainCard():
        this.currentCard = null   // card stays inside the machine

    method returnCard():
        card = this.currentCard
        this.currentCard = null
        return card

    // public API — delegates everything to the current state
    method insertCard(card):              this.state.insertCard(this, card)
    method enterPin(pin):                 this.state.enterPin(this, pin)
    method selectTransaction(transaction): this.state.selectTransaction(this, transaction)
    method ejectCard():                   this.state.ejectCard(this)

// usage
atm = new ATM(bankService, cashDispenser)
atm.insertCard(new Card("1234", "acc-9"))
atm.enterPin("4455")
atm.selectTransaction(new WithdrawTransaction("acc-9", 2000))
atm.ejectCard()
```

**State** is the primary pattern — `ATM` is the context, `ATMState` is the interface, and each concrete state both implements behavior and decides the next state, exactly as in [behavioral-patterns-i](behavioral-patterns-i).

- **Template Method**: `Transaction.run()` fixes the success/failure reporting while `execute()` varies per subclass (withdraw/deposit/inquiry) — same shape as a `DataImporter`.
- **Strategy (optional)**: swap authentication schemes (`PinAuthStrategy` vs `BiometricAuthStrategy`) without touching state classes.
- **Chain of Responsibility (optional)**: hand a withdrawal amount down a chain of denomination handlers (`2000 -> 500 -> 100`) instead of one greedy loop in `CashDispenser`.

Cases interviewers push on:

- **Insufficient ATM cash** — `canDispense()` must check *before* the bank debits the account; if dispensing later fails anyway, compensate with a deposit back (see `WithdrawTransaction`).
- **Concurrent session** — a physical ATM serves one card at a time, so guard the session with a lock on the machine instance; two threads must never both reach `TransactionState`.
- **Card retention** — after `MAX_ATTEMPTS` wrong PINs, retain the card and return to `IdleState` rather than looping forever.
- **Trade-off**: the ATM never trusts a cached balance — every check goes to `BankService`, trading a network round trip for correctness.

blocks.subTitle: Why State for an ATM
blocks.markdown:
⭐ **Q: Why model an ATM with the State pattern instead of a status flag?**

A status flag forces every method to check `if status == X` for every stage, and each new rule touches every method. State pattern gives each stage its own class that only implements the behavior valid there — you structurally can't withdraw cash from `IdleState` because that class never wires up a withdraw path, not just a runtime check.

blocks.subTitle: Dispensing the right notes
blocks.markdown:
⭐ **Q: How do you dispense the correct note denominations for a withdrawal?**

`CashDispenser.breakInto()` walks denominations largest-first (greedy) and takes as many of each as the tray has and the remaining amount allows. If it can't zero out the amount — say only 100s are left for a 2500 request that also needs a 2000 note the tray lacks — it returns null and the transaction fails before any cash moves, so the account is never debited for a dispense that can't happen.

blocks.subTitle: Handling wrong PIN attempts
blocks.markdown:
**Q: How do you handle repeated wrong PIN entries?**

`CardInsertedState` keeps its own `attempts` counter. Each failed `enterPin()` increments it; hitting `MAX_ATTEMPTS` retains the card and drops back to `IdleState` instead of ejecting it, matching real ATM behavior. Because the counter lives on the state instance, it resets naturally the next time a card is inserted and a fresh `CardInsertedState` is created.

blocks.subTitle: Where the bank backend fits
blocks.markdown:
**Q: Where does the bank backend fit into this design?**

`BankService` is an interface the ATM calls for every balance-changing or PIN check — the ATM holds no source of truth of its own, so it can never be tricked by a stale local balance. This also means the ATM works offline for nothing: no network, no transactions, only whatever is cached for display.

blocks.subTitle: Keeping it thread-safe
blocks.markdown:
**Q: How do you keep this design thread-safe for one physical machine?**

Lock the `ATM` session so only one thread drives state transitions at a time — two threads must never both reach `TransactionState` for the same machine. `BankService.withdraw()` must also be atomic on the bank's side, since the same account could be hit from a different ATM or a mobile app concurrently; the lock on the machine alone doesn't protect the account.
